statement: In triangle $ABC$, point $D$ lies on side $\overline{BC}$ so that $AB = AD = DC$. If $\angle BAC = 99^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ABC$?

choices.misconception: I found $\angle ACB = 27^\circ$ correctly and then gave that angle instead of $\angle ABC$.
I assumed $\overline{AD}$ cuts $\angle BAC$ exactly in half, $49.5^\circ$ each, which made $\angle C = 49.5^\circ$, and then I took $180 - 99 - 49.5$.
I treated triangle $ABC$ as isosceles with $AB = AC$, so I computed $\frac{180 - 99}{2}$.
I said the exterior angle $\angle ADB$ equals $x$ instead of $2x$, so my angle sum gave $180 - x = 99$ and I answered $x = 81$.

hints: Mark the equal lengths. How many isosceles triangles can you find?
Let $\angle C = x$. Triangle $ADC$ has $DA = DC$, so $\angle DAC = x$, and the exterior angle $\angle ADB$ equals $x + x = 2x$. Triangle $ABD$ has $AB = AD$.
So $\angle ABD = \angle ADB = 2x$ and $\angle BAD = 180^\circ - 4x$. Then $\angle BAC = (180^\circ - 4x) + x = 99^\circ$.

solutions.reliable: Let $\angle ACB = x$. Since $DA = DC$, triangle $ADC$ is isosceles and $\angle DAC = x$. The angle $\angle ADB$ is an exterior angle of triangle $ADC$, so $\angle ADB = x + x = 2x$. Since $AB = AD$, triangle $ABD$ is isosceles and $\angle ABD = \angle ADB = 2x$, so $\angle BAD = 180^\circ - 4x$. Then $\angle BAC = \angle BAD + \angle DAC = 180^\circ - 3x = 99^\circ$, so $x = 27^\circ$ and $\angle ABC = 2x = 54^\circ$. Check: $54^\circ + 99^\circ + 27^\circ = 180^\circ$.
